biggestGap: Re-author all 24 warden sprites at 48x48 with a 10-12 colour budget, and drop every display scale to an integer multiple of that new master: grid art box 96px (x2, it fits the existing 98px plaque), sheet portrait 96px (x2 inside the 108px frame), Rite portrait 192px (x4, unchanged pixel size, four times the pixel count). Right now every warden is authored at 24x24 -- a QUARTER the area of the SMALLEST monster class in this repo's own art bible (reference/ffvi-art.md S1: small monster 32x32-48x48, medium ~88x64, boss 96x96-128x160) -- while the wardens are the game's boss-tier collectibles. There is no headroom left on that canvas: 15 of the 24 sprites already have a bounding box exactly 24px wide, i.e. they are touching both edges, and the set averages 8.0 unique colours against the doc's own measured 10-12 for a real FFVI sprite. Every downstream failure is a symptom: the Rite magnifies a thumbnail x8 into a 192px lavender blob, the sealed grid is twelve unreadable abstract shapes, and Sulmara's eyes have to be two 3x3 gold bricks because there is no room to draw an eye.
evidence: CRITIC VERDICT, judged from pixels. Replaces the builder self-assessment that scored itself 82. Six screenshots captured at 390x844 @2x over CDP, in progress/shots/wardens-codex-r2-critic-*.png, plus live DOM measurement over CDP and independent PNG decoding of all 24 shipped sprites.

R1's AUTOMATIC LOSS IS GENUINELY CLOSED -- verified my own way, not by trusting the builder's audit. Decoded all 24 bound PNGs off disk and binned every lit pixel (alpha>=128, L>=0.10) by hue: 0 off-axis pixels out of 5,599. Every sprite's mean hue is inside gold 28-60deg or violet 238-296deg; the only sprite that reads '??' is Tessivar at a mean of 74deg, and that is a bimodal gold+violet average, not a stray. r1 spanned 21 distinct 10deg bins across six hue families including literal green at 107deg. Whole-screen census of the BOUND grid confirms it: 0.00% off-axis across 7 bins.

BUT THE ACCENT RATIO IS INVERTED AGAINST THE REFERENCE, AND THAT IS THE NEW PALETTE TELL. Same saturated+lit census run on reference/shots/ui-bar.png: gold 5.64%, violet 1.69% -- the bar is a GOLD screen with violet as a spot accent, 3.3:1 gold-to-violet. Our ALL grid is violet 13.76%, gold 4.19% -- 3.3:1 the other way, eight times the reference's violet load. Twenty-four violet portrait wells tiled down the page is what does it. A purple-dominant collection screen is the gacha cliche; gold-dominant is the premium tell. Not a loss on its own, but it is the reason the grid still reads generic at a glance.

THE BLIND A/B IS DECISIVE AND THE TELL IS THE ART LAYER, NOT THE CHROME. Composite in progress/shots/wardens-codex-r2-critic-ab.png: our BOUND grid, the reference, our Rite, labels stripped. The reference is identifiable in under a second. The specific tell: in the reference NOT ONE ICON ON SCREEN IS FLAT -- the QUEST sword has a blade highlight and a shadowed fuller, the PRESTIGE shield has a raised boss and a beveled rim, the coin has a rim and an inner face, the milestone diamond is a double line with mitred corners, the nav helmet is a modeled 3D object. In ours the SUMMON plate is a genuine match for CLAIM, and then every other gold and violet object is a single flat fill: the nav glyphs are solid one-colour house/oval/anvil/diamond silhouettes, the currency chip icons are flat rings, the rarity pips are flat 4px squares. The reference's smallest icon -- the 8.7K orb, roughly 40px -- carries more rendered depth than our 192px Rite portrait.

THE SUMMON MOMENT IS STILL NOT AN EVENT. progress/shots/wardens-codex-r2-critic-rite.png. Nimreth at x8 is a lumpy lavender-and-white mass with no face, no anatomy and a 3-step ramp; it reads as a crumpled mitten. The 'ritual seal' resolves to two near-white hairline circles at 1px, clipped by both screen edges, which read as render artifacts rather than ornament. Measured the layout live: .summon__domain bottom sits at y=539 and the closing rule top at y=632, so 93px of dead ground still pools in one pocket under the identity block (better than r1's ~200px, not solved). The brief allows this one screen to become an event; it is currently a static portrait on black.

THE SEALED GRID IS THE PROOF SHOT FOR THE CANVAS PROBLEM. progress/shots/wardens-codex-r2-critic-grid-sealed.png: twelve locked wardens read as a comma, a jagged crown, a triangle, a wide V, a lumpy mountain, a bird-ish thing, a blob, an X, a heart, a cat, a bat and a circle. The states themselves are correctly built -- but there is nothing to withhold when the silhouette never resolved in the first place.

SPRITE FORENSICS, THE NUMBERS BEHIND THE INSTRUCTION. Per-sprite unique colours: mean 8.0, min 6 (ossuline), max 10 -- against reference/ffvi-art.md S3's measured 10-12 for a real FFVI sprite. Opaque coverage mean 48.9%, up to 65% (ythra). Bounding boxes: 15 of 24 measure exactly 24px wide, i.e. edge-to-edge with zero margin. Display chain: one 24x24 master rendered at x3 (72px grid), x4 (96px sheet) and x8 (192px Rite). FFVI never magnifies -- it authors at the display size. Eight-times magnification of a thumbnail is why the money shot is a blob.

WHAT GENUINELY HOLDS -- DO NOT TOUCH THE CHROME. Measured live at 390x844: grid is 3 columns of 114x117 on 12px row AND column gaps; document and inner .screen scroller both report scrollWidth 390 == clientWidth 390, zero horizontal drift; every sprite renders at exactly x3.000 from natural 24x24 with image-rendering:pixelated, and no filter or opacity ever touches one (the locked state is a separate PNG, which is the right call); ZERO controls under 44px across grid, sheet and Rite -- r1's 114x36 SUMMON and 117x30 tabs are fixed; sealed card names measure rgb(196,200,202), which is the reference's #C4C8CA secondary to the digit, so locked cards are not faded into illegibility; body ground is rgb(3,10,18) against the reference's #050A10.

RARITY-BY-VALUE IS BUILT CORRECTLY AND IS THE BEST STRUCTURAL IDEA IN THE PIECE. The portrait well is a five-rung OKLab lightness ladder -- L 0.172 / 0.202 / 0.257 / 0.322 / 0.404 for 1-5 pips bound -- and each sealed tier sits exactly one rung under its bound twin (0.160 / 0.183 / 0.228 / 0.279 / 0.343). That is the reference's 'depth by value shift, no glow spam' rule executed properly, and it is why a 24-cell grid does not collapse into flat mush despite the violet dominance.

THE DETAIL SHEET REMAINS THE STRONGEST SCREEN IN THE PROJECT. progress/shots/wardens-codex-r2-critic-sheet.png: diamond-interrupted rules top and mid, an octagonal chamfered gold portrait frame, gold serif VHARNYS, letter-spaced violet ASCENDANT with five pips, a chamfered beveled ASCEND plate, checkpoint rungs on gold and violet diamond bullets. Both of the reference's signature ornaments get their second real use exactly as the brief asked. Only two nits: the flavour line is excellent and the sheet's own portrait is still the 24px master at x4.

MATH IS EXACT. Cross-checked warden-data.js XP_TABLE against reference/melvor-math.md at every published checkpoint: 1,154 at 10; 4,470 at 20; 13,363 at 30; 101,333 at 50; 737,627 at 70; 5,346,332 at 90; 13,034,431 at 99 -- zero drift, and xp(77)/xp(70) converges to 2.000. The live sheet is internally consistent too: Vharnys at bond 62 shows 356,072/368,599 = 64.0%, and the 34,795 ascension cost equals xpAt(63)-xpAt(62) exactly, honouring the stated 1:1-from-the-pool rule. One copy inconsistency: the sheet footnote reads '-10% checkpoint' while the r2 notes describe a 25% checkpoint discount.

NAMING IS CLEAN -- NO AUTOMATIC LOSS. Grepped wardens.html, warden-data.js, wardens.js, wardens.css and make-wardens.mjs against ~45 FFVI character, esper and place nouns. Every apparent hit is the English word 'shadow' inside a comment about shading. All 24 warden names are invented.

RAW HEX IS CLEAN IN OWNED FILES, BUT THE MANDATED GATE STILL CANNOT SEE THEM. `npm run verify` reports 20/20 including 'no raw hex outside tokens.css', yet tools/verify.mjs line ~74 still iterates a hardcoded list of exactly three files (base.css, primitives.css, home.css) and never opens src/styles/wardens.css or wardens.html. I ran the check myself against all four shipped warden files with comments stripped: zero hex literals in any of them. So r1's 13 leaks are genuinely gone -- but the gate that is supposed to prove it remains blind to this entire piece, and that blind spot will silently pass the next piece too.
